issues: hmm-model-block negative control does not exercise the intended state-by-state value comparison. The mutation edits the state-1 emission (2.07294 -> 2.37294), MAP index (1 -> 2), consensus residue (l -> m) and insert line, but simultaneously truncates the final match state with a matching LENG edit, and every recorded failure for that submission (hmm_header, hmm_model, domtbl_profile_consistency) is the parse-level line-count message 'model block has 1201 lines, expected 1200' (controls[8], probe 'hmm-model-block'). Because parse_hmm aborts at the line-count branch, none of the mutated model-block values were ever token-compared, so rejection of a well-formed scientific error in the model body (wrong emission score, wrong exact-integer MAP index, wrong consensus residue, wrong insert line at an intact 3+3*400 layout) is not demonstrated by any executed mutation. The probe author's concerns note acknowledges the conflation, but the cited substitute (hmm-terminal-star-to-number) only exercises the '*' token-identity path, not the numeric tolerance path. Repair by splitting the probe into a value-only model-block mutation that preserves the 1203-line layout, with fresh full execution of all controls on the revised candidate.

Candidate private rationale describes the third execution as 'independent (probe)' and '/work/alternative (independent proxy)', but the recorded solution uses the same pyhmmer 0.12.3 Builder/Pipeline library as the reference (independent_solution/rationale), executed without answer access (independent_execution, LuxC.hmm 3a7c93b3..., 187243 B). This is a same-stack reproduction supporting determinism and answer isolation, not an implementation-independent confirmation; the wording should be corrected (the public/addendum text correctly avoids claiming implementation independence).

question_issues.evidence: The HMMER ASCII writer that produced the reference states this directly: pyhmmer-0.12.3 sdist, vendor/hmmer/src/p7_hmmfile.c lines 2091-2096, printprob() emits -logf(p) of the stored emission/transition/composition probability in %.5f natural-log units ('*' for p==0, 0.00000 for p==1), and p7_hmmfile.c lines 573-623 feed hmm->compo, hmm->mat[k][x], hmm->ins[k][x] and hmm->t[k][x] directly to it with no background division. Log-odds are formed only later in the Plan7 profile (vendor/hmmer/src/p7_profile.c). The reference file confirms it carries #-GF-annotated cutoff/statistics values and node-0 transition values such as 0.01473 = -ln(0.98539), i.e. negative natural-log probabilities of model parameters, not log odds. The base question therefore attaches a false unit/scale description to the compared quantities; a solver reproducing the values as log-odds would be scientifically wrong, and the false label must be corrected (e.g. 'negative natural-log probabilities of the model parameters') rather than excused because all controls pass.
question_issues.quote: Values are the natural units of the format (log odds expressed as negative log probabilities scaled per HMMER convention; `*` denotes zero probability).

Source coverage is complete (13 source operations accounted; the two terminal results are exactly the exported LuxC.hmm and LuxC.domtbl; print(ali) is presentation-only display of already-computed hits), and answer isolation is solid: the answer fixtures pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm and tests/data/msa/LuxC.hmmalign.sto were removed with a controller receipt on this run, remaining LuxC-named files are byte-identical required inputs or inert (verified in the installed tree and the hash-verified release source), no answer literals (domtbl target identifiers, 553.3, 2e-169, 1.989990) appear in installed Python source, and the CKSUM literal 395769323 embedded at test_plan7/test_hmm.py:38 is a deterministic esl_msa_Checksum of the supplied input alignment, not withheld science. However, two defects block packaging: (1) the base question falsely describes the profile's numeric values as 'log odds' when the HMMER writer prints negative natural-log probabilities of the model parameters (verified against the installed vendor source); and (2) the hmm-model-block negative control's executed rejection occurs only through the structural line-count branch, so a well-formed wrong emission/MAP/consensus value in an intact 1203-line model block is never demonstrated as rejected. Both are repairable within the existing contract; revise, not block.

source_coverage.rationale: All 13 recorded source operations (source_operations/operations, faithful to inputs/original.py) are accounted for in the materialization ledger exactly once: two supplied-input reads (MSAFile of data/msa/LuxC.sto, SequenceFile of data/seqs/LuxC.faa), construction machinery (Alphabet.amino, Builder, Background, Pipeline with all-default parameters), the two scientific results with their writers (build_msa -> hmm.write for LuxC.hmm; search_hmm -> hits.write format='domains' for LuxC.domtbl), two stream-opening support calls, and two presentation-only expressions (hmm.consensus inspection and print(ali)). Every terminal scientific product of the converted source is exported verbatim by inputs/exports.py, so nothing eligible is missing. The print(ali) exclusion is justified from the source itself: it queries the already-computed TopHits (hits[0].domains[0].alignment) as an API demonstration, with its hit's scores, coordinates, E-value and posterior accuracy carried in the domain-table row serialized by the retained hits.write call; it is not persisted, exported or consumed downstream, and the full hmmalign alignment (the removed fixture) was never a product of this source path. No invented analysis, changed method or silent endpoint omission is present; the default-parameter claims in the brief match the pipeline's defaults per the vendored HMMER sources. The false 'log odds' units label in the base question is reported in question_issues rather than here, since it misdescribes the requested values without discarding any endpoint.
